title: libtorrent deprecated settings are compiled out of the default ABI-2 build
claim: DEPRECATED_SET expands to { name, fun, default } only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION==1 and to { "", nullptr, 0 } for ABI 2 and for any other value; CMakeLists.txt:739-742 makes TORRENT_ABI_VERSION=2 the default build (option deprecated-functions DEFAULT ON), so coalesce_reads, coalesce_writes and aio_max are registered with an empty name and a null callback and no settings_pack key of that name is usable; include/libtorrent/settings_pack.hpp:465-489 shows the coalesce_reads enum names exist only under TORRENT_ABI_VERSION==1, and a grep of src/*.cpp finds no consumer of coalesce_reads/coalesce_writes/aio_max outside settings_pack.cpp
limitations: setting index still exists so a stale client can write a value nothing reads

title: libtorrent per-peer runtime request window (m_desired_queue_size)
claim: runtime work allowance: m_desired_queue_size = int64(request_queue_time) * download_payload_rate / block_size, then clamped into [min_request_queue=2, m_max_out_request_queue]; the recomputation is skipped entirely while m_slow_start is true (slow start grows the window per received piece instead); a snubbed peer is pinned to 1 before this code runs (src/peer_connection.cpp:4802-4806)
conditions: requires an associated torrent for block_size
limitations: a single peer's allowance, not a session allowance

title: libtorrent effective window collapses to 1 in end-game and for snubbed peers
claim: desired_queue_size() returns 1 when m_endgame_mode or m_snubbed is set, otherwise returns m_desired_queue_size; the value consumed by the request path is therefore not the computed runtime allowance in those two states

title: libtorrent max_out_request_queue is a per-peer hard cap
claim: m_max_out_request_queue is initialised in the peer_connection constructor from settings_pack::max_out_request_queue (default 500) and the only mutator is max_out_request_queue(int); a grep of src/peer_connection.cpp shows the mutator is never called from anywhere else, so no runtime path raises the cap above the configured value
limitations: cap/allowance pair with S-CODE-LT-011: the settings key is the ceiling the runtime formula is clamped to

title: libtorrent request_timeout() is an adaptive timeout with the configured value as ceiling
claim: request_timeout() returns m_settings request_timeout (60 s) only when m_request_time has zero samples; with one sample it returns avg+avg/5; with two or more it returns avg+4*deviation; the millisecond result is divided by 1000 with rounding up, capped at the configured request_timeout and floored at 2 seconds
limitations: floored at 2 s so the granularity is whole seconds

title: libtorrent send buffer watermark computed per fill cycle
claim: buffer_size_watermark = uploaded_last_second * send_buffer_watermark_factor(50) / 100, then raised to at least send_buffer_low_watermark (10240) and lowered to at most send_buffer_watermark (512000); the runtime watermark therefore tracks recent upload rate inside the configured band
limitations: runtime value not observable through settings_get

title: libtorrent end-game entry condition in request_blocks
claim: dont_pick_busy_blocks = ((strict_end_game_mode && picker.get_download_queue_size() < picker.num_want_left()) || queue sizes non-zero); set_endgame(true) is only reached after the picker failed to fill num_requests and the peer is not choked, so duplicate (busy-block) requests only start when the swarm cannot supply a free block

title: libtorrent rate_based_choker recomputes the slot count and bypasses unchoke_slots_limit
claim: unchoke_sort reads unchoke_slots_limit (8; negative means unlimited) but when choking_algorithm == rate_based_choker it resets upload_slots=0 and re-derives it by sorting peers by upload rate and adding one slot per peer whose rate exceeds a threshold that starts at rate_choker_initial_threshold(1024) and grows by a hardcoded 2048 B/s carrying the comment TODO: make configurable; the configured unchoke_slots_limit is then not honoured
conditions: only when rate_based_choker is selected; default is fixed_slots_choker
limitations: slot growth step is not configurable

title: libtorrent round-robin seed choking quota rule
claim: unchoke_compare_rr keeps already-unchoked peers ahead until they have been unchoked for more than minutes(1) and have received more than piece_length * seeding_piece_quota(20) bytes since being unchoked; then they are de-prioritised
limitations: quota measured in pieces so it scales with piece size

title: libtorrent piece priority levels and the hardcoded partial-piece cap
claim: download_priority_t constants: dont_download=0, low_priority=1, default_priority=4, top_priority=7; pick_pieces() forces prioritize_partials when num_partials > num_peers*3/2 or num_partials*blocks_per_piece > 2048, the latter carrying the comment TODO: 2 make the 2048 limit configurable
conditions: 2048 blocks equals 32 MiB at the 16 KiB default block size
limitations: partial-piece cap is hardcoded

title: libtorrent connection_speed quota handed out per tick and halved by smooth_connects
claim: try_connect_more_peers returns immediately when num_connections() >= connections_limit; otherwise it hands out connection_speed(30) attempts round-robin, first deducting outstanding torrent_connect_boost connections, and when smooth_connects is true it caps the quota at (remaining_slots+1)/2; hence attempts per tick <= connection_speed and <= half the remaining connection slots
limitations: number of ticks per second is tick_interval driven

title: libtorrent connections_limit plus connections_slack is the admission ceiling
claim: incoming connections are rejected once num_connections() >= connections_limit + connections_slack (200 + 10 at defaults) and outgoing attempts stop at connections_limit itself; connections_slack is the only headroom above the configured cap
limitations: cap/allowance pair with S-CODE-LT-020: the settings keys are the ceiling; the per-tick quota is the runtime allowance

title: qBittorrent skips the removed coalesce_reads settings on libtorrent 2 builds

title: qBittorrent-Enhanced-Edition third-party branch retains the same connection-limit override

limitations: optional corroboration only

title: Transmission 4.2.0 rechoke pulse period
claim: tr_peerMgr declares static constexpr BandwidthTimerPeriod = 500ms, PeerInfoPeriod = 1min and RechokePeriod = 10s; the rechoke timer is started repeating at RechokePeriod in the constructor (peer-mgr.cc:1113).

title: Transmission 4.2.0 rechoke-now marshalling
claim: rechokeSoon() shortens the rechoke timer to 100ms for an immediate pulse; rechoke_pulse_marshall() runs rechoke_pulse() then restores the interval to RechokePeriod (10s), so a new peer forces one early rechoke instead of waiting the full 10s.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 rechoke_pulse scope
claim: rechoke_pulse loops every running torrent and calls rechokeUploads(swarm, now) plus updateInterest(swarm) only when swarm->stats.peer_count > 0; torrents that hit their seed limit are stopped first.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 unchoke slot count
claim: rechokeUploads breaks out of the sorted choked list as soon as unchoked_interested >= session->uploadSlotsPerTorrent(), i.e. the number of unchoked interested peers is capped by the session setting, not by a per-peer constant.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 optimistic unchoke
claim: OptimisticUnchokeMultiplier = 4; the swarm's optimistic_unchoke_time_scaler is decremented on every rechoke pulse and the optimistic peer is cleared when it reaches 0, so an optimistic unchoke survives 4 rechoke calls; one new random interested peer below the slot cutoff is unchoked only when s->optimistic == nullptr and not maxed out.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 throttle-aware rechoke
claim: is_maxed_out = s->tor->bandwidth().is_maxed_out(tr_direction::Up, now); when upload is maxed out each candidate keeps its previous choke state (item.is_choked_ = item.was_choked_) and no new optimistic unchoke is made, so the unchoke decision is coupled to the bandwidth scheduler's is_maxed_out(), not only to peer ranking.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 choke ordering and seed choking
claim: ChokeData's ordering prefers higher rate, then previously-unchoked peers, then prefers interested peers; rechokeUploads chokes upload-only seeds in one pass, chokes everyone if choke_all (torrent cannot upload), and salts ties with tr_salt_shaker before std::ranges::sort(choked).

title: Transmission 4.2.0 default peer limits
claim: Defaults are TrDefaultPeerLimitGlobal = 200 and TrDefaultPeerLimitTorrent = 50; SessionSettings initialises peer_limit_global = TrDefaultPeerLimitGlobal (200) and peer_limit_per_torrent = TrDefaultPeerLimitTorrent (50).

title: Transmission 4.2.0 peer limit enforcement
claim: A new swarm peer is rejected when swarm->peerCount() >= swarm->tor->peer_limit(); enforceSwarmPeerLimit closes all but the `max` most active peers; enforceSessionPeerLimit counts tr_peerMsgs::size() across torrents and partial_sorts by ComparePeerByMostActive, closing everything past the global limit.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 peer-info target count
claim: get_max_peer_info_count(tor) returns tor.peer_limit() when the torrent is done, otherwise tor.peer_limit() * 3U; candidate-list/peer-info retention is a multiple of the configured hard peer limit.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 client request queue (reqq)
claim: SessionSettings.reqq defaults to 2000U; tr_session::reqq() returns it; tr_peerMsgs advertises it to peers as the BEP-10 `reqq` extension value in the handshake map.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 block size
claim: TrBlockSize = 1024U * 16U = 16384 bytes and tr_block_info::BlockSize aliases TrBlockSize; all arithmetic derived from blocks (request estimation, buffer floors) is in 16 KiB units.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 per-peer desired request count
claim: max_available_reqs() computes min(ceil, max(estimated_blocks_in_period, Floor)) where Floor = 32 blocks, Seconds = RequestBufSecs = 10s, estimated_blocks_in_period = piece-download-rate * 10s / 16384, and ceil = peer-supplied peer_reqq_ or PeerReqQDefault = 500; so an unconstrained peer is allowed 32 to 500 in-flight blocks depending on measured speed.
conditions: peer_reqq_ is set only when the remote advertises reqq>0 (peer-msgs.cc:1468-1472)

title: Transmission 4.2.0 request pipeline cap
claim: update_desired_request_count() assigns desired_request_count_ = max_available_reqs(); maybe_send_block_requests() returns early when active_req_count(ClientToPeer) >= desired_request_count_, otherwise asks for exactly (desired_request_count_ - n_active) blocks via tr_peerMgrGetNextRequests.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 upload-side request admission
claim: can_add_request_from_peer() rejects an incoming block request when std::size(peer_requested_) >= client_reqq() (the session reqq, default 2000), logging 'rejecting request ... reqq is full'; otherwise the request is queued and the output buffer is filled.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 peer-io upload buffer floor
claim: The peer-io upload target is max(Floor, current_speed * PeriodSecs) with PeriodSecs = 15s and Floor = static_cast<uint64_t>(tr_block_info::BlockSize * 3.5) = 57344 bytes, so each peer buffers at least 3.5 blocks ahead of its measured upload speed.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 bandwidth per-direction allocation
claim: allocate_bandwidth() iterates {tr_direction::Up, tr_direction::Down} and, only when band_[dir].is_limited_ is true, sets bytes_left_ = desired_speed_.base_quantity() * period_msec / 1000; it is invoked from tr_bandwidth::allocate(period_msec) which the peer manager calls every BandwidthTimerPeriod = 500ms, so a limited direction gets half its per-second desired speed per pulse.
conditions: unenforced direction (is_limited_ false) leaves bytes_left_ as-is (unlimited)

title: Transmission 4.2.0 bandwidth round-robin scheduling
claim: tr_bandwidth::allocate() buckets peerIos into three arrays by priority (high/normal/low, with high also counted as normal and normal also as low), then runs phase_one(peers, Up) and phase_one(peers, Down) per array; phase_one shuffles peers, gives each peer Increment = 3000 bytes of flush() per pass and rotates out peers that cannot use the full increment, until bandwidth or peers are exhausted.
conditions: Increment = 3000 bytes chosen so a uTP full-size frame can be sent immediately

title: Transmission 4.2.0 parent bandwidth clamp
claim: tr_bandwidth::clamp(dir, byte_count) first limits to the local band_[dir].bytes_left_ when is_limited_, then recursively applies parent_->clamp(dir, ...) when band_[dir].honor_parent_limits_ is true, so child (per-peer/torrent) quotas are nested inside the session quota.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 default speed limits are disabled
claim: SessionSettings defaults speed_limit_down_enabled = false and speed_limit_up_enabled = false while speed_limit_down = 100U and speed_limit_up = 100U; the numeric 100 values are inert placeholders, so out of the box both directions are unthrottled (no limit), matching the 0=unlimited convention at the API level.
conditions: the 100 values only take effect once the corresponding *_enabled flag is set

title: Transmission 4.2.0 hard cap vs dynamic request quota
claim: The configured peer limits (global default 200, per-torrent default 50) are hard admission caps enforced by rejection at peer-mgr.cc:1630 and by enforceSessionPeerLimit closing the least-active excess, independent of how much work any single peer is allowed.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 runtime work quota recomputed per pulse
claim: The actual per-peer work allowance is not a config constant: desired_request_count_ is recomputed each update from measured piece speed (rate * 10s / 16384, clamped to [32, peer reqq or 500]), so a peer can be connected under the hard cap yet granted only 32 in-flight blocks.
conditions: requires metainfo and not done and client interested/unchoked

title: Transmission 4.2.0 webseed connection limiter
claim: ConnectionLimiter allows MaxConnections = 4 parallel web tasks; after any failure max_connections() drops to 1, data received resets failures and clears the pause, and MaxConsecutiveFailures = MaxConnections = 4 failures pause the webseed for TimeoutIntervalSecs = 120s.

title: Transmission 4.2.0 webseed request sizing
claim: on_idle() requests spans from tr_peerMgrGetNextRequests(&tor, this, max_blocks) and truncates to max_spans; max_available_reqs() returns 0 when slots_available()==0 and otherwise {max_spans = n_slots, max_blocks = n_slots * PreferredBlocksPerTask} with PreferredBlocksPerTask = 64, so up to 4*64 = 256 blocks per idle wake.
conditions: the comment calls the value 64 arbitrary

title: Transmission 4.2.0 webseed task prefetch buffer
claim: Each tr_webseed_task holds content_ of type tr::StackBuffer<tr_block_info::BlockSize, std::byte, std::ratio<5,1>> (5 * 16 KiB = 80 KiB) and request_next_chunk() issues one HTTP range fetch per file chunk (min bytes left in file, bytes left in task) starting at the current file offset.
